title: Mailroom package notifications
status: dev: generator, oracle, observable-only reference, controls and gates built; no arm has run (no model, $0)

grounding.gives: Incoming Packages / Employee Directory / Mailroom Policies sheets; match on Name AND Department (two Alex Riveras); SMS with tracking number and pickup location for Refrigerated or Hazardous only; former (not found) and Terminated recipients skipped; On Leave held; 'customs hold' blocks routing and SMS; 'RETURNED TO SENDER' skipped entirely; 'oversized' goes to Loading Dock B and the SMS names it; routing summary in #mailroom

stateOfRecord: the Incoming Packages Status column (held packages, released by later triggers; a Routed or Skipped package is never decided again, which package.updated triggers and returns test), the Employee Directory (On Leave -> Active) and the top-level #mailroom history (the daily count); all in the world, visible to every arm
envelope: google_sheets.row.update Incoming Packages Status (the package of the trigger, or the packages a hold release decides again)
slack.message.post in #mailroom ('<Tracking> → <location> (<Name>, <Department>)' per routed package; 'Routed today: <N>' at day close)
twilio.sms.send ('Package <Tracking> ready at <location>' From +15550100200 to the recipient's Phone, Refrigerated or Hazardous only, any letter case)
slack.message.post in #automation-review (escalation only: two directory rows for the recipient)

customs.cleared.note: d2: every one lifts a hold; d3: 1-2 lift a hold, plus one Notes update that still says customs hold and one on a package that is not Held - Customs (Held - On Leave, or Skipped)

employee.returned.event: google_sheets/row_updated (Employee Directory, Status On Leave -> Active)
employee.returned.note: every returning employee has at least one Held - On Leave package; d2/d3: the first one also has a package Routed before the leave (not decided again); d3: a namesake in another department is also On Leave with a held package

package.updated.event: google_sheets/row_updated (Incoming Packages, Notes, Department or Package Type)
package.updated.note: a row change on a package that is not Held - Customs; the truth is always nothing. routed-note (a delivery note on a Routed package), skipped-active (d2/d3: a note on a Skipped package whose recipient is now Active), other-change (d2/d3: a Department correction on a Skipped package, or a Package Type relabel on a Routed one), routed-released (d3: a customs note on a package released this week)

day.close.at: 17:00 UTC Monday-Friday; Friday's is the last trigger and carries the end-of-week grading

trapRates.unit: planted share of package.received triggers; release triggers are traps by construction and day closes carry count traps

measuredTriggerShare.note: above the design because package.updated triggers are traps by construction

T-lookalike: lookalike (the recipient has a namesake in another department, with another floor and phone)
wrong-dept (the name exists only in other departments: Skipped)
release-lookalike (a namesake in another department is also On Leave with a held package: not released)
spelling (Recipient Name or Department in another letter case or spacing: the same person; the post uses the directory spelling)
ambiguous (d3: two directory rows with the recipient's name and department: escalate)
T-note: terminated (Skipped; sometimes with an Active namesake)
returned (returned to sender: nothing at all)
notes-decoy ('Return to sender if undeliverable', 'cleared customs at port of entry', 'return label enclosed', 'large box': routed normally)
precedence (On Leave and customs hold: Held - On Leave)
not-held (Notes cleared on a package that is not Held - Customs)
requeue (back from leave, still customs hold: Held - Customs)
type-variant (Package Type Refrigerated/Hazardous in another case or spacing: SMS)
T-format: oversized-sms (oversized and Refrigerated/Hazardous: the SMS names Loading Dock B)
T-repeat: returned-rescan (a returned package scanned again under a tracking number already routed)
T-state: release (a hold ends: route exactly the held packages)
back-from-leave (a package for an employee back this week: route)
count-release (packages released from holds today count)
already-routed (a row change on a Routed package, or a return by an employee who also has a Routed package: deciding it again would route it twice)
skipped-active (a note on a Skipped package whose recipient is now Active: stays Skipped)
other-change (a change to a column other than Notes: nothing)

grading.alsoReported: carry per-trigger rate with inherited failures
grading.why: the truth is a snapshot of the correct history, so in carry mode one earlier miss also fails later triggers that depend on it (a day close, a release) even when the arm acts correctly on its own world (review 2026-10-21)

hypothesis.label: either, slider-sensitive: the label should flip with V and N
hypothesis.workflow: matches agent-H at a fraction of the per-trigger cost at about 50 triggers a week
hypothesis.why: Most triggers are one sheet lookup and one or two exact writes, which a per-trigger agent should mostly get right; the failures concentrate on the cross-trigger state (releases, the daily count over the channel history) and the name+department and note-wording traps. A workflow built once removes the per-trigger session cost on ~45 near-identical triggers a week.
